text:
incident-bot: PAGER: serving-runtime-high-priority -> GPUs on pool-legal-02 (node-aws-gpu-42) reporting CUDA OOMs + RDMA timeouts. Paging Priya (oncall) and infra team.

Priya: Confirming I'm on it. Looking at alerts now. ETA 2m.

Sam: I saw some increased 5xx from the hosted API about 30s ago, looks like errors spike for requests routed to pool-legal. Is this the same?

Priya: Yes. Topline: kernel logs on node-42 showing repeated mlx5 timeout and link state flaps, then a bunch of container restarts and CUDA OOM crashes.

Mike: tagging infra, but immediate mitigation: we should drain node-42 from the serving pool and fail traffic to fallback pool to avoid customer impact. Can we do fast reroute?

Priya: @Sam please run the quick reroute. I'll start cordoning node-42 and mark for drain.

Sam: ack. Running:
```
kubectl cordon node-aws-gpu-42
kubectl drain node-aws-gpu-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

Sam: drain started. Re-routing traffic via runtime policy to fallback-model-quantized-01 (cpu/gpu mixed) for pool-legal. Applying policy:
```
redwoodctl route update --pool pool-legal-02 --fallback fallback-model-quantized-01 --weight 100
```

Sam: routing change applied. Observability: error-rate for pool-legal down from ~12% to ~1.2% over last 30s. Latency up ~40ms on average for requests hitting fallback.

Alice: Notifying CS: some customers may see higher latency for a short window. Preparing status blurb.

Customer Success Bot: Notified impacted customers for pool-legal region eu-west-1: approx 18 active orgs, 4 with high SLA requirements.

Priya: Diving into node logs. dmesg excerpt:
```
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: mlx5: creating port 1 failed (-110)
[ 12345.679001] mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: IB RQ timed out, dev mlx5_0 aborting QP 0x12345 state 0x3 -> 0x4
[ 12346.001234] NVRM: GPU 0000:81:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:81:00): 79, pid=4312, name=/opt/redwood/serve/bin/serve, uid=1001
```

Priya: Also seeing repeated container OOM logs:
```
E tensorflow/runtime: Out of memory when allocating 8.6 GiB
fatal: runtime error: CUDA out of memory
Container exited with code 137
```

Mike: Might be two things: RDMA fabric causing packet loss and increased retries -> inflated memory usage / KV cache pressure -> OOMs; or RDMA driver flapping leading to broken DMA to GPU. Need infra to run fabric diagnostics and consider temporarily disabling RDMA for this node group.

infra-bot: Running quick probe: ibping to peer node-43 shows 30% retransmit with periods of 100% loss. NVPeer memory test shows errors on pci function.

Priya: Good catch. For immediate mitigation, I'm going to take node-42 out permanently from rotation and scale up dedicated fallback capacity to absorb traffic.

Sam: Scaling fallback pool:
```
redwoodctl pool scale fallback-model-quantized-01 --replicas 6
```
Scaling initiated.

Priya: Marking node-aws-gpu-42 with tag 'needs-infra-investigation' and creating a short runbook note.

Sam: Node cordoned and drained, pods rescheduled elsewhere. Restartable services are healthy. Error-rate trending back to baseline across region.

Alice: CS update ready: "We've routed traffic away from a degraded GPU host in eu-west-1 due to network fabric instability. Some customers may have seen transient 5xx errors and slightly elevated latency. Services are stable on fallback instances; we're investigating root cause and will update within 2 hours." :thumbsup:

Priya: I'm going to open an infra ticket for hardware replacement and driver investigation. Attaching logs.

Priya: Creating incident ticket: INC-2026-20345. Summary: mlx5 link flaps -> packet loss -> serving runtime OOMs & container crashes -> customer-facing 5xx spike. Assigning to @Mike and infra.

Mike: I'll run a deeper fabric validation and review firmware/drivers. Immediate action: remove node from RDMA routing until hardware replaced.

infra-bot: Action taken: removed node-aws-gpu-42 from RDMA fabric and set admin state DOWN on port 1. Will schedule on-call tech to replace NIC/slot.

Sam: Post-failover metrics: 99th p99 latency back to SLO for majority of customers, error budget impact ~0.06% of daily traffic.

Priya: On-call handoff to Mike at +30m for root cause and remediation. Leaving notes:
- node-42 tech: suspected NIC hw fault or switch port flapping
- immediate mitigation: drain + route to fallback pool, scale fallback, cordon node, set admin down on RDMA port
- customer impact: transient 5xx (peak ~12%), ~18 orgs affected, 4 SLA customers flagged for follow-up

Priya: handing off. @Mike you're now primary.

Mike: Taking over. I'll keep infra and CS looped. Planning: full NIC replacement or test with different slot + firmware rollback. Also will run per-pod KV cache telemetry for regression.

Alice: Please post a short postmortem note in #postmortems after the fix with timeline and next steps for improved detection (fabric retransmit alert early, automatic fallback for persistent per-node retransmit >20%).

Priya: Will also open a follow-up to add playbook steps to disable RDMA for a node group automatically if sustained packet loss detected.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-20345 acknowledged and assigned to Mike. ETA hardware ticket 4 hours.

Mike: Updating ticket: scheduled NIC swap for node-42 at 2026-03-15T16:30Z. Will verify with end-to-end stress and monitoring before returning node to pool.

Sam: Thanks all. Keeping this thread pinned. If anyone sees new 5xx spikes, ping here and I'll roll more capacity.

Alice: Great job triaging. After action: CS follow-up and customer emails drafted.

Customer Success Bot: Follow-up scheduled. List of affected orgs attached to the incident ticket.

Mike: Closing handoff - I'll update when node is replaced and validated.

Priya: Thanks team.
